column1: # candor framework-reach table — GENERATED by soundness/kappa_table/derive.sh; DO NOT EDIT (SOUNDNESS R492/R727).
# owner.name+desc <TAB> effects: in every surveyed artefact declaring the owner, the statically-resolved body
# reaches a body this engine's scan charged with those effects (direct, concrete only). A member with NO row
# is not claimed pure: it keeps the treatment it had without this table.
# NAMED MISS: the closure stops at the JDK, which is OPAQUE here (no bodies; only the classifier's name rules),
# while framework bodies are TRANSPARENT. A framework member whose effect happens inside a JDK body the
# classifier leaves uncharged is missed exactly as a direct call to that JDK member is (R814 is that frontier).
# hedge: J = a JDK package (runtime), S = a surveyed framework class, A/U = a framework member the
# table cannot vouch for (A: no body — dispatch; U: the scan read it only as Unknown, or the
# previous table had a line for it and its body still carries Unknown — the R1189 floor — or its bodies carry
# Unknown and the closure reaches no concrete effect, R1193). See FrameworkReach.
# P = a member a NAME rule charges whose surveyed body is a proven-pure field accessor (R1052).
# O = a public member overridden in ANOTHER surveyed jar by a body that can do more than the row says;
#     the overriding classes follow (R1097). See FrameworkReach#crossJarOverriders.
# H = a surveyed class's DIRECT supertypes (superclass first, then interfaces; Object omitted), so a consumer
#     scan can tell that its own class reaches a framework type THROUGH a framework class (R1509).
# T = a member of a subclassable surveyed class whose body (and the bodies it runs on the same receiver) calls
#     back an overridable member on `this`; the number of the L line listing those members follows (R1511):
#     `via>member` (reached through the body of `via`, an overridable member; empty for the called member's own),
#     or `p<i>:owner.member` (dispatched on the called body's i-th parameter).
#     Written only where it differs from what the walk up the H lines' first entries reads. See Cha#templateCallbacks.
# Y = the same for a member of a surveyed INTERFACE whose DEFAULT body a consumer class implementing it runs;
#     walked over Y lines alone, so a T and a Y line never answer for each other (R1574). See Cha#inheritedFrameworkInterfaces.
# L = a numbered list of T/Y entries, members named by M number; M = a numbered member (R1511).
# D = a member whose body, closed over what it runs (the scan's own `calls`), dispatches on an abstraction a
#     CONSUMER can implement -- a receiver it can supply (a field, an element, a wrapped argument); the number of
#     the E line listing those members follows. E = a numbered list of K numbers; K = a numbered dispatched member
#     (R1565/R1569). The consumer joins its own implementers of each, as it joins a chained row's `dispatchesOn`.
# C = a member whose closure reaches a dispatch the table cannot follow, where a NAME rule's charge used to
#     stand in for it and no surveyed implementer carries that effect; the unfollowed member follows (R1468).
